newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee soars for 5th straight day.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee soars for 5th straight day.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures soared for the fifth straight day Wednesday, with new contract highs being posted across all delivery months out to May 1998, as hedge buying by roaster and further fund speculation extended the four week old rally.
CSCE March coffee ended up 8.30 cents at 171.85 cents a pound, after seeing a new contract high at 173.00 cents.
"The market is getting nervous, with first notice day for CSCE March coffee next Thursday and still 16,000 contracts of open interest remaining," Refco New York analyst Anne Prendergast said.
"The market will be watching the US Green Coffee Association stocks data due next Monday and the official estimates of the Brazilian crop from that country's exporters next week also."
Concerns about impact of rain on the Colombian crop as well as the impact of a Colombian state workers strike which began Tuesday were also fueling bullish sentiment, analysts said.
Labor leaders billed the strike of 800,000 public sector workers as the biggest in 20 years, which may disrupt exports from the second largest exporter of coffee.
Low consumer stocks have seen the nearby spreads become sharply backwardated, with the CSCE March/May spread jumping to contract highs at 9.55 cents a pound Wednesday.
Clive McKeef, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640;
